proposals.mechanism: chassis_wider_than_gap (bedroom: 23.0 cm overall vs 19.8 cm opening) and battery_exhausted (lawn: 4.08 Wh usable ran out 79% of the way, range 3.87 km < 5 km)
proposals.principle: A robot passes an opening only if overall width plus steering error fits; range is usable energy over energy per metre.
proposals.hypothesis: Tub width 18->11 cm gives ~16 cm overall (+<=1.0 cm steering error) well inside 19.8 cm. Battery 4.8->14.4 Wh (6 cells: 2 in pack + 4 on hand, free) gives 12.2 Wh usable against ~6 Wh needed for 5 km even with +108 g (energy/m ~4.2 J/m). Both are within the current parts' ranges, so no swap is needed.
risks: shed: more mass on the 22 deg ramp, but traction holds to 26.1 deg regardless of mass and stall force 16 N >> ~2.1 N needed
kitchen/living_room/under_sofa: edge climb is friction-geometry, independent of mass and width; height unchanged at 6 cm
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained bedroom, lawn, lost none; costs $0.00, 102 machine min

proposals.principle: Among obstacles a robot may go only as fast as it can stop within its sensing range.

Camera only lights 0.12 m in the dark (< body length); lidar is not provided.
risks: under_sofa: sonar adds no height, so it is safe
lawn energy: +0.08 W is negligible against 2.5 W of electronics

proposals.mechanism: step_higher_than_climbable (porch 5.6 cm vs 2.23 cm max), sinks_in_sand (2.49 kPa sinks 3.38 cm vs 1.17 cm climb-out), gap_longer_than_support (garden: 3 cm wheel drops 5.1 cm into a 9 cm trench)
proposals.principle: A track climbs any edge that meets its sloped front run up to about its front idler height; ground pressure is weight over contact area; a rigid vehicle bridges a gap while its CoM stays over support, about 0.45 of a track's contact length.
proposals.hypothesis: No wheel radius fixes the porch: r=4.5 cm climbs ~3.35 cm. A rocker-bogie needs r>=5.6 cm, which makes it >=13 cm tall and breaks the 9 cm under_sofa. Tracks with a 6.5 cm idler meet the 5.6 cm edge and stand 8.0 cm tall (<9 cm sofa). A 28 cm contact length bridges ~12.6 cm > 9 cm trench. A ~170 cm2 patch gives ~0.3 kPa (est.), sinking ~0.4 cm < 2 cm belly. The 1.8 cm sprocket on 2 x 100:1 N20s (on hand) gives ~0.56 m/s and ~13 N, ample for the 22 deg ramp and all time limits.
risks: under_sofa: total height 8.0 cm vs 9.0 cm overhang; 1 cm margin. If the fit loop needs it, idler 6.0 (7.5 cm tall) still exceeds the 5.6 cm edge
shed: heavier and higher rolling resistance, but stall ~13 N vs ~3 N needed; grousers grip gravel at least as well as rubber tyres
kitchen/living_room: small steps (0.8-1.5 cm) are far below the idler height; 5 m at ~0.56 m/s is ~9 s of 40 s
lawn (if gained by proposal 1): tracks raise J/m; with 12.2 Wh usable it should still cover 5 km, but the margin is thinner
bedroom (if gained): tracks add their own width per side; with an 11 cm tub it should still fit 19.8 cm
proposals.result: refused before trial: the track frames mount on the tub's sides: a 28.0 cm track needs a tub 24.0-32.0 cm long; it is 20.0 cm

proposals.edit: locomotion -> tracks (idler_height=6.5, track_length=26); chassis (length=26, ride_height=2, width=11); battery -> liion_pack (capacity=28.2)
proposals.mechanism: step_higher_than_climbable (5.60 cm edge vs 2.23 cm wheel climb), gap_longer_than_support (9 cm trench vs 6.0 cm wheel span), sinks_in_sand (2.97 kPa on 15 cm2 sinks 4.02 cm vs 1.17 cm climb-out)
proposals.principle: A track climbs any edge meeting its sloped front run up to about its front idler height; a rigid vehicle bridges a gap up to ~0.45 of track contact length; sinkage falls with ground pressure = weight / contact area.
proposals.hypothesis: No wheel radius fixes any of the three: r=4.5 climbs ~3.35 cm and spans 9 cm with no climb-out margin, and its patch stays tiny; rocker-bogie needs r>=5.6 cm (>=13 cm tall, breaks under_sofa 9 cm). Tracks with a 6.5 cm idler meet the 5.6 cm porch edge and stand 8.0 cm (<9 cm sofa). A 26 cm contact bridges ~11.7 cm > 9 cm trench. ~200 cm2 contact at ~0.6 kg gives ~0.3 kPa, ~0.4 cm sinkage in sand. The tub is lengthened to 26 cm because the refused iteration-1 proposal showed track frames need a tub within ~4 cm of track length. One motor per side means 2 of the 4 on-hand 100:1 N20s are used; the 1.8 cm sprocket gives ~13 N of pull for ~6 N of weight and ~0.56 m/s no-load. The Li-ion swap (28.2 Wh, 138 g, lighter than six NiMH cells at 162 g) covers the lawn: at ~0.5 m/s, electronics energy per metre roughly doubles and track rolling resistance is higher, so the 5 km survey would need ~12.5 Wh, more than the 12.24 Wh the NiMH pack can supply.
risks: under_sofa: track height 8.0 cm vs 9.0 cm overhang, only 1 cm margin
bedroom: track frame width is unknown; overall width ~16-17 cm plus ~1 cm steering error must fit the 20 cm opening offset 2 cm (System 1 can steer the line through it)
lawn: top speed falls to ~0.56 m/s no-load; ~0.45 m/s under load gives ~11,000 s for 5 km vs 14,400 s allowed; energy is covered by the 28.2 Wh pack
shed: 22 deg ramp needs ~2.8 N of the ~13 N available, and the tracks' grousers hold better than wheels on gravel
hallway: slower but 11 m at ~0.5 m/s takes ~22 s vs 45 s; the 2 m sonar range is ample
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained garden, porch, sandbox, lost none; costs $29.00, 193 machine min

proposals.principle: Track front run climbs edges up to its idler height; the bridge length is ~0.45 of contact length; a larger contact patch lowers ground pressure and sinkage.
proposals.hypothesis: Cheaper variant ($14, keeps the NiMH pack): a 7 cm idler gives more margin over the 5.6 cm porch edge, and a 28 cm contact bridges ~12.6 cm over the 9 cm trench. The tub is set to 28 cm to fall within the 24-32 cm the frames require. It tests whether the lawn energy budget holds without the battery change.
risks: under_sofa: 8.5 cm tall vs 9.0 cm overhang, 0.5 cm margin
lawn: 12.24 Wh usable may fall short with heavier, slower tracks (~12.5 Wh estimated), and it is also time-limited at ~0.45 m/s
bedroom: unknown track width at the 20 cm opening
